name: Question 2
problem:
$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

Given the inner product on the set of continuous functions over $x\in [0,2\pi )$ defined above, select the correct options below.$\,$
$⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)⟩=$
{{field-1}}

$\,$
The functions $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)$ 
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
We begin by using the half-angle identity

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡(6x)=\frac{1}{2}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(12x)).
$$

Substituting this into the integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x),\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(12x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{1}{24}\operatorname{sin}⁡(12x)]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\pi -0)+\frac{1}{24}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(24\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)$ and $g(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)$ $\text{are not orthogonal}$ with respect to the inner product.

EXPLANATION

We begin by using the half-angle identity cos2⁡(6x)=12(1+cos⁡(12x)).

Substituting this into the integral gives ⟨cos⁡(6x),cos⁡(6x)⟩=∫02πcos2⁡(6x)dx=∫02π12+12cos⁡(12x)dx=[12x+124sin⁡(12x)]02π=12(2π−0)+124(sin⁡(24π)−sin⁡(0))=π.

Therefore, f(x)=cos⁡(6x) and g(x)=cos⁡(6x) are not orthogonal with respect to the inner product.
